brief:
Israeli property purchases in Exarchia, a historically pro-Palestine neighbourhood in central Athens, are intensifying local grievances over gentrification and housing affordability, Al Jazeera English reported. Residents blame short-term rental listings by foreign investors for rapid rent increases and the erosion of the district's character as a bohemian and activist hub.

The influx of Israeli buyers has become a flashpoint in a neighbourhood long defined by left-wing politics and solidarity activism. Long-term residents report being priced out as properties are converted to tourist accommodations, transforming the once tight-knit community into a transient tourist zone.
dek: In Exarchia, residents say short-term rentals are driving up rents and eroding its character.
title: Israeli buyers fuel housing tensions in Athens's pro-Palestine district
